diagrams.title: **One agent per user, one memory drawer per agent
diagrams.caption: **One agent per user, one memory drawer per agent.** The numbers match the six steps below. Notice the code labels: each agent's memory tool is already pointed at one user before the conversation starts.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 600" aria-label="Personalised agent architecture. Users Mona Mona and Bunny Kaushik send requests. The Strands Agents SDK creates one agent per user with create_agent. Each agent has its own mem0_memory tool bound to its user ID, mona_mona or bunny_kaushik. Mem0 stores user preference memory in a FAISS index on disk, partitioned by user. A system prompt sets personalised responses, restricted memory access and web search use. The agent calls Amazon Bedrock (Claude Sonnet 4.6), uses a DuckDuckGo web search tool for live information, and returns personalised answers. diagrams.title: **Extract, compare, store; then search by meaning
diagrams.caption: **Extract, compare, store; then search by meaning.** Because facts are compared with what's already stored, Mem0 can update an old preference instead of piling up contradictions.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 400" aria-label="Inside Mem0. Store path: the user's text goes to an extraction LLM (Claude Haiku 4.5) which pulls out short facts. Mem0 compares them with similar existing memories and decides ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or no change. New facts are embedded with Titan v2 and saved in the FAISS index under the user's ID. Retrieve path: a query is embedded, and a vector search inside that user's memories returns the closest facts." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>

diagrams.title: **Put the wall in code, not in words
diagrams.caption: **Put the wall in code, not in words.** On the left, the model decides whose memory to open, so clever wording can change its mind. On the right, the decision was made before the conversation began; there's nothing for the prompt to argue with.
